# Sappurisa Sutta (MN 113 (PTS MN iii 37))

**ID:** MN 113 (PTS MN iii 37)  
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Sappurisa Sutta  
**Title (English, from literature):** A True Person  
**PTS:** MN iii 37  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul1.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul1.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sappurisa Sutta* ("A True Person" or "The True Man") is the 113th discourse of the *Majjhima Nikāya* (PTS MN iii 37) [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995]. In this discourse, the Buddha distinguishes the character of an untrue person from that of a true person, explaining that a truly good person does not disparage others or feel conceited and superior on account of their attainments or qualities [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995; Anālayo 2014]. The text sets out a detailed list of spiritual and ascetic qualities, meditative states, and attainments in relation to which conceit is to be avoided, including being learned, knowing the discourses, and knowing the Vinaya [Anālayo 2014]. In dealing with progressive meditative stages, the sutta explains that the training enables a practitioner to hold aloof (*atammayo*) and shed all tendencies toward imaginings or conceiving (*maññanā* / *maññati*), continuing up through the cessation of perception and feeling (*saññāvedayitanirodha-samāpatti*) [Ñāṇananda 1971; Shulman 2010].

Direct parallels to MN 113 are found in the Chinese Āgamas: MĀ 85 (titled the *Scripture of the True Man*, *Chen jen ching*), an individual translation cataloged as Taishō 48 (*Sat-puruṣa-sūtra*), and EĀ 17.9 [Tsukamoto 1979; Hahn et al. 1997]. While the Pāli text and T 48 warn against pride in being learned in the discourses and Vinaya, MĀ 85 adds the study of Abhidharma to this list [Anālayo 2014].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: EA 17.9; MA 85 真人; T 48 是法非法

**Sources**

- [Anālayo 2014] Bhikkhu Anālayo, The Dawn of Abhidharma (2014) — Discussion of the avoidance of conceit regarding recitation of discourses, Vinaya, and Abhidharma in the sutta and its parallels.
- [Hahn et al. 1997] Michael Hahn, Jens-Uwe Hartmann, and Konrad Klaus (eds.), Bauddhavidyāsudhākaraḥ (1997) — Identification of T 48 as a translation parallel to the Sappurisa-sutta.
- [Ñāṇananda 1971] Katukurunde Ñāṇananda, Concept and Reality in Early Buddhist Thought (1971) — Analysis of holding aloof and overcoming maññanā up to saññāvedayitanirodha in MN 113.
- [Tsukamoto 1979] Zenryu Tsukamoto, A History of Early Chinese Buddhism (1979) — Noting the correspondence between MN 113 and Madhyamāgama 85 (Chen jen ching).
- [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995] Bhikkhu Ñāṇamoli and Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Middle Length Discourses of the Buddha (1995) — English translation title 'The True Man' and summary of distinguishing the true from the untrue man.
- [Shulman 2010] Eviatar Shulman, 'The Sati-paṭṭhāna-sutta on Mindfulness, Memory and Liberation' (2010) — Citation of MN 113 (MN iii 45) regarding the cessation of conceiving (maññati) in saññāvedayitanirodha.
